title: A World Without Up or Down
text: Have you ever wondered what would happen if you let go of your pencil and it just stayed there in the air? Or if you tried to pour water and it formed floating blobs? This isn't magic—it's what life is really like in space!

title: What do you think?
text: If you throw a ball straight up in the air here on Earth, it always comes back down. Why do you think the same ball would just float away in a spaceship?

content.title: Floating in Space
content.description: An astronaut floating weightlessly inside the space station.

title: The Secret is Microgravity
text: In space, astronauts experience something called microgravity (often called zero gravity). This happens because the spacecraft is constantly falling around the Earth, making everything inside it feel weightless!

content.description: The condition in which people or objects appear to be weightless.
The invisible force that pulls objects toward each other, like Earth pulling you down.

content.question: What happens if you spill a glass of water inside a spacecraft in space?
options: It falls straight to the floor.

content.title: Teach Your Sibling
content.text: Try explaining to your younger sibling or a friend why astronauts have to strap themselves to their beds when they sleep!

title: Connecting the Dots
text: Think about magnets! Just like a big magnet pulls small iron nails toward it from a distance, Earth uses gravity to pull us toward its center, even though we can't see the force.

content.title: Space Inventor Challenge
content.text: Design a special lunchbox for astronauts. How would you stop the dal from floating away? Draw your design and label its parts!

content.title: Teaching Tip
content.text: Remind students that gravity still exists in space! The reason astronauts float is because they are in continuous free-fall orbit around the Earth.

content.title: Zero Gravity vs Microgravity
content.text: Many people think there is absolutely ZERO gravity in space. In reality, gravity keeps the moon and space station in orbit. It's actually microgravity that makes them feel weightless!

title: Why Don't People Fall Off the Earth?
text: Look at a globe. If you are standing in India, someone in Argentina is exactly on the opposite side. Why don't they fall off into space? Are they hanging upside down?

title: What would happen?
text: Imagine the Earth was shaped like a giant flat plate. What would happen to the oceans at the edges?

content.title: Gravity Pulls to the Center
content.description: Arrows showing gravity pulling everything towards the core of a spherical Earth.

title: The Big Pull
text: There is no 'up' or 'down' in space! Down is simply the direction gravity pulls us—toward the center of the Earth. So people in Argentina feel perfectly upright, just like you!

content.question: Which way is 'down' for someone standing on the opposite side of the Earth from you?
options: Towards the stars in the sky.
Towards the center of the Earth.
There is no down for them.

content.title: Imagine It!
content.text: Close your eyes and imagine the Earth as a giant magnet pulling your shoes to the ground. How would walking feel if the magnet was suddenly turned off?

title: Cosmic Connections
text: The same force (gravity) that keeps you from floating off the Earth is what keeps the Moon orbiting around the Earth, and the Earth orbiting around the Sun!

content.title: Gravity Map Challenge
content.text: Draw a large circle representing Earth. Add tiny stick figures at the top, bottom, left, and right sides. Draw arrows showing which way 'down' is for each person.
